conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that EMDR therapy can alleviate PTSD symptoms, citing robust evidence from randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and major health organizations like the World Health Organization and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: Yes — EMDR therapy can alleviate PTSD symptoms, and the evidence supporting this is robust.**

Multiple randomized controlled trials (RCTs), systematic reviews, and meta-analyses confirm EMDR's effectiveness for PTSD. A Cochrane-informed systematic review published in *Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews* (2020) concluded that the growing body of RCTs supports a "confident recommendation of CBT-T and EMDR as the first-line treatments" for PTSD in adults ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32284821/); [Cochrane](https://www.cochrane.org/th/evidence/CD003388_psychological-therapies-chronic-post-traumatic-stress-disorder-ptsd-adults)).

Major health organizations endorse EMDR based on this evidence. The **World Health Organization** recommends EMDR (alongside CBT) for people suffering from PTSD, noting these techniques help reduce vivid, unwanted recollections of traumatic events ([WHO, 2013](https://www.who.int/news/item/06-08-2013-who-releases-guidance-on-mental-health-care-after-trauma)). The **U.S. VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline (2023)** recommends individual trauma-focused psychotherapy — specifically including EMDR — over medications for PTSD ([PTSD: National Center](https://www.ptsd.va.gov/professional/treat/txessentials/overview_therapy.asp)). The VA's professional resource also states that "EMDR has the strongest recommendation for being an effective treatment in several clinical practice guidelines" ([PTSD VA.gov](https://www.ptsd.va.gov/professional/treat/txessentials/emdr_pro.asp)).

The **American Psychological Association** does not list EMDR as a strict first-line treatment but indicates it is "probably effective" for adult PTSD ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_movement_desensitization_and_reprocessing)). Some controversy exists regarding its mechanism, but the clinical outcomes evidence is strong and consistent across guidelines.
